evidence: Liv. 8.6: impactus ita est saxō, ut sōpīrētur, he was stunned (Lewis & Short: “became unconscious or senseless”)
terms.comment: To put to sleep, and so to knock someone senseless: the boxer who is knocked out is sōpītus.

evidence: Ter. Ad. 4.2.32: cerebrum tibi (Lewis & Short s.v. dīminuō)
terms.comment: Literally “to smash someone’s skull”: in comedy a threat of violence (Plaut. Men. 2.2.30 caput hominī), not of stunning. Traupman uses it for a knockout in boxing.

evidence: Liv. 40.45.3: tempestās in Capitōliō aliquot signa cōnstrāvit, “throw down, prostrate (very rare)” (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: diminuo · Lewis & Short: cerebrum
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
